rapport.opening_line: Hey Dave, I noticed you run an independent air shop in Indy — I work with a lot of distributors on the treatment side of their compressor sales.
rapport.adapted_script: You know he's an independent distributor but not his exact brand lineup or whether he already carries a dryer/filtration line. Your discovery has to fill those gaps: ask what he sells, how he handles treatment on a compressor sale today, and whether he drop-ships dryers. If he drop-ships (likely), the margin gap is your opening — frame KSI as a line he'd OWN with real margin, a treatment attach on every compressor, and Midwest lead-feed. Confirm territory before promising leads and confirm he's not locked to a manufacturer. Products: ECOTROC KTA-S refrigerated, ECOTROC DDAP desiccant, ECOCLEAN APF filtration. Don't assume the pain — surface it first.
watch_outs: Revenue and employee data may be stale — verify, don't cite
Don't assume he drop-ships or that he has no dryer line — ask before pitching the fix
He's a 22-year trade veteran — talk distributor economics, don't oversimplify
SCOPE: KSI's line here is dryers and filtration ONLY — keep the recommendation to those
product_reference: ECOTROC KTA-S — refrigerated dryers, 14 to ~1,890 CFM, ~$1,880 up to ~$47,000. The everyday attach on a compressor sale if he'll carry the line.
ECOTROC DDAP — desiccant dryers for low-dewpoint / critical air. Higher ticket, higher margin.
ECOCLEAN APF — coalescing + particulate filtration, ~$155 to ~$709 per housing. Recurring consumable pull-through.
The angle if he drop-ships today: real margin on a line he OWNS vs. cost-plus-nothing catalog drop-ship, plus KSI lead-feed + co-marketing in his corridor.
German-engineered — reliability protects the service reputation of a shop that lives on callbacks.
